graphEvents.label: Which fixtures and metrics separate a missed command from a wrongly started one
Existing command tests are inventory tests, not behavior tests
Six command metrics separate recall from unsafe runs

label: The labeled corpus has 195 rows across true_write, true_read_only, memory_save_resume, mixed_ambiguous, deep_loop_prompts and skill_routing_prompts; none is keyed to the six command groups, so create, design, doctor and prompt regressions have no direct row.
The calibration baseline covers 200 rows with Brier 0.204829 and expected calibration error 0.138314, and measures skill confidence quality, not command surfacing.
The release gate is skill-level: holdoutTop1, per-skill accuracy and UNKNOWN counts; no schema field counts command recall, command precision, ask decisions or unsafe starts.

Existing command tests are inventory tests: command-metadata-e2e asserts projection and file existence, and command-bridge-resolution-guard asserts bridge slash ids resolve; neither measures what a prompt returns.
The doctor family has the right proof shape: doctor-phrase-reach.cjs checks each admitted phrase reaches its route; no equivalent exists for the other five groups.

A complete fixture set needs three row types per group: a plain-chat recall row, a near-miss discrimination row against a competing skill, and a read-only or refusal row that must not start a mutating command, plus chat-only, partial-slash, quoted-slash and child-session variants.

The metrics that separate the failure classes are commandRecall@1 and commandPrecision, unsafeRunRate, askRecall and askPrecision, skillCommandAgreement and childAutoStartRate; a missed command is a recall failure with a silent brief and a wrongly started command is a precision or unsafe-run failure with a visible brief.
Command rows should live in a separate harness: the calibration Brier and ECE are tied to the 200-row corpus hash, so adding rows would make a routing regression look like a calibration change.

direction: Reusing the skill accuracy gate as the command gate
reason: It has no command class, so a command miss scores the same as a skill miss
